newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN RUPIAH STABLE IN SLOW LATE TRADING.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN RUPIAH STABLE IN SLOW LATE TRADING.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in late trading on Friday, dealers said.
They said trading was slow, with the market shrugging off a central bank interest rate cut in the morning.
"There was sporadic trading but we didn't see much impact from the interest rate cut," one European bank dealer said.
Dealers said the cut was not a surprise as a previous rise was seen as a temporary measure to contain speculative dollar buying in the aftermath of currency turbulence.
On Friday, the bank cut all bilateral SBIs above one-week by 50 basis points while maintaining high overnight rates.
The bank kept overnight bilateral SBIs at 14.0 percent and four-to-six day at 15.0 percent.
The central bank remained absent from the short-term securities (SBPUs) market and also did not offer repos on SBIs.

The bank cut seven-day bilateral SBIs to 9.5 percent from 10.0 percent, two-week to 10.0 percent from 10.5 percent, one-month to 10.625 from 11.125, three to 10.5 from 11.0, six to 11.125 from 11.625 and one-year to 11.75 from 12.25 percent.
Spot rupiah was at 2,597.0/2,600 at 0920 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,585.0/93.0. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,596.5/99.5 and 2,593.0/95.0, respectively.

"Sentiment is a bit mixed on the rupiah. There is no clear direction, with some local players still looking for dollars although foreigners kept selling," the European bank dealer said. "The rate cut had no immediate impact on the spot or swap market. But it did turn the stock market around."
He said the stock market recovered from Thursday plunge following the rate cut, but slid back before the close.
The dealer said the money market was still cautious on rupiah liquidity because very short-term papers remained expensive.
However, the rate cut drove longer-term interbank rates lower while overnight money eased on sufficient supply although it fluctuated briefly on state bank purchases.
Overnight money ended at 14.5 percent against 16.0 percent at the opening. One-month money was at 16.50/17.00 and three at 17.50/17.75 percent.
One-month swap was at 18.0/18.5, two at 40.0/42.0, three at 59.0/64.0 and six at 115.0/125.0 points.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,378/2,682 but raised the conversion band to 2,573/2,621 on Friday from 2,567/2,615 on Thursday. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
